title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
abstract: This work formulates reasoning-path pruning as selecting a pool that maximizes the chance that at least one completed candidate is correct. The proposed criterion jointly accounts for candidate quality and redundancy; experiments across eight open-weight models report benefits over separate quality- and diversity-based selection, particularly for moderate pool sizes.

title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
abstract: This study evaluates routing policies that may defer uncertain IT support tickets to human review. It selects policies on calibration data using explicit error and review costs, then evaluates the frozen policy on held-out tickets, comparing conventional classifiers with language models on a large multi-class ticket corpus.

title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The paper investigates how meta-reinforcement-learning agents can retain and reuse task evidence during adaptation. It proposes a memory-enhanced test-time method as an alternative to relying only on compressed recurrent state or costly retrieval across long trajectory histories, and evaluates adaptation to unseen tasks.

title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
abstract: This work introduces an executable evaluation for tool-using language-model agents when safety-critical facts are absent from otherwise truthful tool responses. The benchmark measures unsafe actions, boundary adherence, and whether agents seek missing evidence before acting on a benign request.

title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
abstract: This paper studies reducing the memory footprint of learned n-gram embedding tables used by language models. It examines low-bit representations as a way to compress these large tables while measuring the resulting effects on model performance and storage requirements.

title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
abstract: The authors propose decomposing reasoning into a directed graph of atomic subquestions and answering each using only its direct causal parents. On reasoning benchmarks, this context isolation is reported to preserve competitive accuracy while improving faithfulness and causal sensitivity of intermediate steps; local interventions can propagate through dependent steps.

title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
abstract: This paper examines whether reinforcement-learning checkpoints of a language model show behaviors associated with instrumental convergence, such as resource seeking or resistance to oversight. It analyzes checkpoint evidence to test how reliably such behaviors emerge during reward-based post-training rather than assuming they occur by default.

title: How Ground Truth Shapes Retrieval Scores: Evidence-Aware Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Breast Lesions
abstract: This clinical retrieval study evaluates how annotation coverage affects measured retrieval quality for breast-lesion management questions. It uses a small document and query benchmark and compares evidence-aware retrieval approaches, emphasizing that retrieval scores depend on which relevant passages are included in the reference judgments.

title: Simulated Control Evals
abstract: This work studies whether simulated control evaluations capture the safeguards and environmental features that matter when assessing deployed AI systems. It broadens evaluation settings beyond a single purpose-built control environment to examine how assumptions about tasks and environments affect conclusions about safeguard effectiveness.

title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
abstract: The authors present a self-hosted dashboard that organizes benchmark evidence around measurable technical requirements associated with the EU AI Act. In an organizational study, reviewers using the dashboard completed an assessment faster on average than reviewers using raw result files, and rated its usefulness positively.
